about: The stdout stream of `hyprial gui [dev] --json`: newline-delimited compact JSON objects. Line 1 is the startup record (ok:true) or a failure (ok:false), except that with --stdin-stop a stop requested before the record exits 0 with NO stdout line. After a startup record the process stays in the foreground; at most one more line may follow, a failure explaining why the session ended. Nothing else is written to stdout; progress and warnings go to stderr. Keys not listed under startupRecord.required are informational and may change without a version bump.

exitStatus.0: the host exited 0, or a --stdin-stop request (EOF or a `shutdown` line on stdin) was honoured; a stop requested before the startup record is written exits 0 with empty stdout, which a consumer must read as a clean stop, not a protocol error
exitStatus.2: the command line was refused before anything started
exitStatus.other: the host child's own exit status

stream.stop: SIGTERM, SIGINT, or with --stdin-stop an EOF or `shutdown` line on stdin. Only this invocation's process groups are reclaimed; the daemon is left running.
stream.secondLaunch: the same home and driver fails with GUI_RUNTIME_BUSY and data.runtime naming the directory
stream.neverContains: the launch grant, the upstream bearer, server.json content or any credential-bearing URL

consumerChecks: url parses with scheme http, a loopback literal host and the same port as the port field
host is the host of url and port is the port the host bound (never 0)

handoff_path, when present, is absolute on the consumer's own platform and names a regular file owned by the caller whose single line is `<url origin>/#grant=<percent-encoded grant>`; on POSIX the file has mode 0600, on Windows there is no mode bit and the file's privacy rests on account-private directory access (see homeAdmission), not on 0600; the file is one-time and the host removes it on consumption, expiry and stop
a consumer refuses a record_version larger than the one it knows

handoff_path.description: An absolute path in the host platform's form: POSIX `/...`, or on Windows a drive-letter path (`C:\...`, `C:/...`) or a UNC path (`\\server\share\...`). Relative, drive-relative (`C:x`) and rootless (`\x`) paths are refused. A consumer also checks that the path is absolute on its own platform.

backend_owned.description: true only when this launch started a backend child it will stop (the contract-mock driver); false for the daemon driver, whose daemon outlives the GUI and is never stopped by it.

codesNote: Codes a consumer should expect on a failure line; not a closed set.

homeAdmission.requirement: Before identity reads, daemon startup or runtime creation, the selected home must pass the kernel private-directory check: current owner and mode 0700 on POSIX, account-private access on Windows.
homeAdmission.effects: Read-only refusal; does not chmod, take ownership, start a daemon or replay a credential write. Existing overly broad directories require explicit operator correction. Runtime permission changes after admission remain checked by credential writers.

startup.business: daemon through the request-http v1 dispatch inside the same-origin Python session host
startup.note: Foreground installed GUI: the Python session host serves the verified built-in assets and relays the daemon through the request-http v1 dispatch in its own process; hyprial gui ensures the daemon. The handoff opens this launch only and is not E2E acceptance.
startup.handoff_note: Open the absolute URL in this private 0600 file.
